cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Fake the Expertise
cards.instruction: Perform expertise so confidently that no one questions you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I'll get your boiler running. I know these controls.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've been adjusting the kitchen timer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Establishing the heating interval. Call the engineer; I'll need someone on the boiler.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He asks what temperature you measured.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell him we're still establishing the baseline. Put him on speaker; I'll ask the questions so he can concentrate on readings.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 asserts expertise and decision power, A3 postpones scrutiny, and A5 takes over questioning so the engineer becomes a subordinate data supplier.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 timer correction causes A3 invented heating-interval explanation; B4 measurement query causes A5 baseline evasion and question control.

relationship.evidence: B2 identifies a real mistake and B4 relays an engineer practical question, giving A performance credible pressure.

heightening.evidence: B4 expert inquiry threatens exposure; A5 elevates the bluff into directing the actual expert work.

specificity.evidence: A1 boiler problem, B2 kitchen timer and B4 measurement request establish what A does not competently address.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 letting the engineer concentrate on readings masks ignorance as management, with modest repetition in A3 preface.
